title: Development of sustainable food packaging films by modifying polyvinyl alcohol with carboxymethyl cellulose and montmorillonite clay
content: The development of a pivotal and sustainable system for packaging applications is in high demand. In the present work, we engineered polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) with the natural polysaccharide cellulose-derived carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) and montmorillonite clay (MMT) to develop an environmentally friendly food packaging material. Biodegradable polyvinyl alcohol/carboxymethyl cellulose/montmorillonite (PVA/CMC/MMT) films were developed via a casting route. The effective incorporation of CMC and MMT into the PVA matrix has been confirmed by XRD, FTIR spectroscopy and SEM analysis. The incorporation of both CMC and MMT did not significantly alter the transparency of PVA. The effective reinforcement offered by CMC and MMT was revealed from water vapour transmission rate (%), mechanical properties and dynamic mechanical analysis. Compared to virgin PVA, the PVA/CMC/MMT system showed inhibition of a representative Gram-negative bacterium, Escherichia coli (E. coli), as examined by the disc diffusion method. Soil burial degradation data showed that the system exhibited an excellent degradation rate. The incorporation of CMC improved the biodegradation rate; as the CMC concentration reached 1.5 wt%, the % degradation was found to be 78%. To evaluate the performance of the developed nanocomposite films as an active packaging material, wrapping studies were conducted using strawberries. Overall, the PVA/CMC/MMT films offer a highly competitive system exhibiting good water resistance, excellent biodegradability, superior mechanical properties and optimal transparency, indicating their potential application in food packaging.
